record.context_brief: Stability of a greedy server on a circle
record.original_question: A single server moves on a circle. Particles arrive according to a Poisson process of rate lambda and are placed uniformly on the circle. Serving a particle takes one unit of time, and after each service the server moves at positive finite constant speed to the nearest waiting particle, ignoring new arrivals while moving. Is this greedy-server model stable for every lambda < 1?

evidence.quote: A single server is located on the circle. Particles arrive in a Poisson stream of rate lambda and are uniformly distributed on the circle. It takes a single unit of time to serve a particle. After any service, the particle disappears, the server chooses to serve next the closest particle and moves to it with a positive finite constant speed.
The conjecture is: this model is stable for any lambda < 1.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a single server moving on a circle of finite circumference. Particles (customers) arrive according to a Poisson process of rate $\lambda > 0$ in time, and each arriving particle is placed at a location chosen uniformly at random on the circle, independently of everything else. The server operates as follows:

- Serving any single particle takes exactly one unit of time. While the server is serving a particle, it does not move.
- Immediately after completing a service, the particle being served is removed from the system, and the server selects, among all particles currently waiting, the one whose distance along the circle from the server's current position is smallest (ties broken arbitrarily).
- The server then travels along the circle toward that nearest waiting particle at a fixed positive finite speed $v$. New arrivals occurring during this travel are not considered for re-selection until the server reaches and begins serving the chosen particle.
- Upon arrival at the chosen particle, the server begins serving it (taking one unit of time), and the cycle repeats. If the system is empty when a service ends, the server waits in place until the next arrival, then proceeds toward it.

The system is said to be stable if the underlying Markov process describing the server position together with the configuration of waiting particles is positive recurrent.

Prove or disprove: for every $\lambda < 1$ and every fixed speed $v \in (0, \infty)$, this greedy-server model is stable.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture (originally due to Coffman and Gilbert, 1987) that the greedy server on the circle is stable whenever the service rate exceeds the arrival rate was proven by Rojas-Nandayapa, Foss, and Kroese in "Stability of the Greedy Algorithm on the Circle" (arXiv:1112.2389, 2011), who established positive recurrence for any positive finite speed under the condition λ < 1.

status_evidence.title: Stability of the Greedy Algorithm on the Circle
status_evidence.snippet: We show that the conjecture holds true: the service rate exceeding the arrival rate is a sufficient condition for the system to be positive recurrent, for any value of the speed.
status_evidence.claim: The Coffman–Gilbert conjecture for the greedy server on the circle was proven, establishing stability for all λ < 1 and any finite positive speed.

status_evidence.title: Stability of the greedy algorithm on the circle - WRAP Warwick
status_evidence.snippet: Stability of the greedy algorithm on the circle.
status_evidence.claim: Published version confirms resolution of the stability conjecture on the circle.
